table_section: A typology of sovereign AI
value: A state's capacity to develop, run and govern AI on infrastructure, data and models it controls, rather than renting them from foreign providers. Definitions are contested: 'hard' sovereignty means self-sufficiency across the stack; 'soft' sovereignty means control over the layers that matter for a given use case.

table_section: A typology of sovereign AI
value: Domestic data centres and GPU clusters under national legal control, funded by budgets, state banks or sovereign-wealth vehicles.

table_section: A typology of sovereign AI
value: IndiaAI common compute (38,231 GPUs); Isambard-AI (UK); ABCI 3.0 (Japan); JUPITER (EU)

table_section: A typology of sovereign AI
value: Foundation models pre-trained from random initialisation by a national lab or champion.

table_section: A typology of sovereign AI
value: Falcon (UAE); Jais 2 (UAE); K2 Think V2 (UAE); ALLaM 34B (Saudi)

table_section: A typology of sovereign AI
row: Sovereign models - adapted (continued pre-training / fine-tune of foreign open weights)

table_section: A typology of sovereign AI
value: Foreign proprietary or open models run in-country under local data residency, often via 'sovereign cloud' offers.

table_section: A typology of sovereign AI

table_section: A typology of sovereign AI
value: Legal and practical control over national training corpora and the data pipeline (licensed national-library, news and administrative text).

table_section: A typology of sovereign AI
